metadata.description: Personal Claude Code plugin marketplace by korsicheg

plugins.name: persona-dialog-eval
plugins.description: Persona-dialog evaluation for conversational agents: hold a case (with fixed ground-truth labels) constant and vary only the speaker — persona and language — then have an LLM play that speaker in a real dialog with the actual agent and score its emitted decision (category / team / intent / severity) per persona and language. Scaffolds a complete eval/ (reusable scoring engine + dialog runner + enforced anti-fabrication driving CLIs + guarding unit tests), generates a committed corpus, and produces an accuracy report with a per-expected-value breakdown and a miss list.

plugins.name: clean-code
plugins.description: Robert C. Martin's Clean Code as eleven routing knowledge-base skills: one per language with a solid community adaptation, plus a shared core for everything else. Each is a chaptered reference — rules, worked examples, a cheatsheet, a glossary and a pattern catalogue — and each description routes to the right sibling, so the model loads the one skill that fits the file it is editing; a SessionStart gateway names the dispatch. clean-code-java carries the original book (Java examples, the refactoring case studies, and the 66-item smells-and-heuristics catalogue). Nine skills carry the community adaptations, each worked in its own idiom: clean-code-typescript (TS types, Failable results), clean-code-javascript (closures, promises), clean-code-python (ABCs, dataclasses, mypy), clean-code-php (strict comparison, final classes behind interfaces), clean-code-csharp (properties, records, LINQ, async), clean-code-go (errors as values, small interfaces, scope and mutability), clean-code-ruby (duck typing, keyword arguments, blocks), clean-code-dart (named required parameters, cascades, null safety) and clean-code-swift (protocols, optionals, value types). clean-code-universal is the family's shared core: a language-agnostic distillation built on a three-tier spine that separates rules holding wherever you can name a thing and run a check (Tier 1) from rules binding only where a construct exists — a parameter list, a type system, an exception, a test runner, a thread (Tier 2). It carries the languages without a sibling — Rust, C++, C, Kotlin, Scala — and the declarative ones: YAML (Kubernetes, Helm, CI pipelines), Terraform/HCL, SQL, Bash, Dockerfile, with a translation table stating, per rule, what it means where there are no functions, no classes and no unit tests. Sources and licences differ per skill: see NOTICE.md.

plugins.name: athens-transit
plugins.description: Athens public transport: live OASA bus and trolley times, metro/tram journeys from Google with bus legs made live, the best stop to walk to, when to leave, and leave-now alerts that follow a live location, in the session or through your own messaging command. Each person keeps their own places and Google Maps key.

plugins.name: trip-cost
plugins.description: What a drive in Greece costs: motorway tolls from mydiodia.gr, fuel for your own car at real station prices, where to fill up and stop on the way, and the cheapest stations near any place. Each person keeps their own car profile and Google Maps key.
